records.name: Hive76
records.summary: A makerspace in Kensington where people build and learn with woodworking tools, electronics, laser cutters and 3D printers. Anyone can drop in on a Sunday open house to try the space.
records.what_you_do: Work on your own projects with shared tools and benches. Members pay a monthly fee and sign a liability waiver before they use the space.

schedule.text: Open houses on Sundays from 2 to 5 pm. Members can also come in on their own schedule, depending on their plan.

cost.text: Light membership is $15 a month (equipment during open houses). Basic is $60 a month with 24-hour access. Core is $120 a month with a personal desk.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday open house, or email the group to set up a one-on-one tour
first_step.basis: The site says beginners and experienced makers both use the space, and open houses are a set way to try it.

records.notes: Newest dated news on the home page is a classroom cleanup post from January 25, 2026. Prices are as the group lists them on its site and may change. Ages allowed were not stated, so crowd is set to adults only as a guess from the membership setup; the owner may want to check.

records.name: NextFab
records.summary: A makerspace in North Philadelphia with laser cutters, 3D printers, electronics, sewing, metal and woodworking tools. Classes and shop time need a membership, but you can take a tour first.
records.what_you_do: Take classes, use the tools, and join the member community. Several of its free Repair Fairs are held here.

schedule.text: Open Saturday through Thursday from 10 am to 8 pm. Closed on Fridays. Classes run on their own dates.

cost.text: A membership is needed for most classes and shop access. Class prices are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Take a tour, look at the membership options, then sign up
first_step.basis: Tours are offered, but full access and classes need a paid membership first.

records.notes: Could be read as a business. It is included because it runs a member community, classes and public tours. Owner may decide. The site's events section listed no dates; the activity evidence is that the Philly Fixers Guild calendar lists Repair Fairs at this address in October, November and December 2026. Zip code not stated on the page, so left out. Beginner class prices were not on the classes page.

records.name: Philadelphia Woodworks
records.summary: A woodshop in Philadelphia where beginners and experienced woodworkers take classes, use the shop with a membership, and send kids to woodworking camps and after-school programs.
records.what_you_do: Take one-day or evening classes, learn tools in intro sessions, or join as a shop member. Women can take a women-only shop introduction.

schedule.text: Classes run on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays, mostly during the day, with some evening sessions. The shop is closed on Mondays and Fridays.

cost.text: Classes and membership are priced on the site. A fall sale offers 50 percent off membership and 25 percent off classes for a limited time.

first_step.how: Pick a class or intro session on the calendar and sign up, or email the shop
first_step.basis: The shop lists several intro sessions for new woodworkers, including a women-only shop introduction.

records.notes: Leans commercial (a paid woodshop with a lumber yard and custom millwork), but it has a membership shop and kids programs, so it is included. Owner may decide. The page lists October 2026 dated classes and a Safety Certification on October 17, 2026. Membership eligibility and safety orientation steps are not spelled out on the page. The page gives the address and zip 19128, but does not name a neighborhood.

records.name: Philly Fixers Guild
records.summary: Volunteers who fix broken household items for neighbors at free Repair Fairs around the city. You bring the item, and a volunteer works through the fix with you.
records.what_you_do: Fix items at Repair Fairs, teach the troubleshooting steps, or answer repair questions through Ask a Fixer.

schedule.text: Free Repair Fairs on Thursdays from 6 to 8 pm. Upcoming fairs are October 8, November 12 and December 10, 2026.

first_step.how: Bring a broken item to a Repair Fair, or sign up on the site for fair notices and volunteer information
first_step.basis: Fairs are open to anyone with an item to fix, and the group says skilled and general helpers are both welcome.

records.notes: Fair locations vary; past fairs were held at other places (a farm in Fishtown, a sculpture studio, a food co-op in Kensington), per the home page news list, which had no dates. The volunteer contact details were on a page not captured here. Photo gallery suggests the group was founded around 2014.

records.name: Mid Atlantic Amateur Radio Club (WB3JOE)
records.summary: Ham radio operators in the western Philadelphia suburbs who meet monthly, run weekly radio nets, and help with public service events and exam sessions.
records.what_you_do: Join the monthly online meeting, check into the radio nets, or take part in field days and public service work.

schedule.text: Monthly meeting on the fourth Tuesday at 7:15 pm, held online. Radio nets on Wednesdays and Sundays at 8:30 pm.

cost.text: Dues and fees are not listed.

first_step.how: Email the club to ask for the Zoom link for the next monthly meeting
first_step.basis: Meetings are online and open with a clear way to ask for the link, though the page does not describe a newcomer program.

records.notes: Status is dormant because the newest dated item is an annual report from December 2022. The meeting and net times are undated, so the group may still be meeting; verify before the owner relies on it. The club's own site loaded only as a frame set with no news, so the meeting details come from the ARRL listing. The club says it has about 85 members and six repeaters at three sites. Ham radio license exams are offered; the ARRL listing does not say how often.

records.name: Philly Tech Sistas
records.summary: A nonprofit that helps women of color build coding and tech career skills. It runs beginner workshops, career talks, and mentoring circles.
records.what_you_do: Attend a coding workshop or a career talk, join a mentoring circle, or volunteer as a mentor or teaching assistant.

schedule.text: Workshops, talks and mentoring circles run on a changing schedule. Check the events page or the Meetup group for upcoming dates.

cost.text: Prices are not listed on the website. Check the events page for each workshop.

first_step.how: Join the Meetup group linked from the Join us button, then sign up for a workshop
first_step.basis: The site says it welcomes women who are new to tech, and it lists beginner workshops.

records.notes: Home page is a working site, but it has no dated events, so status is probably active rather than confirmed. Press coverage found in search dates from 2019 to 2020. Mission is serving women of color; community is set to women only as the closest tag. Location and meeting place not stated on the page, so left out.

records.name: Power Up Tech Corps
records.summary: A City of Philadelphia volunteer program that helps residents build online skills, like applying for jobs online and getting in touch with family. Volunteers work in libraries, rec center computer labs and community sites.
records.what_you_do: Monitor a computer lab, help a City Digital Navigator in a class, or teach a lesson from the city's digital skills curriculum.

schedule.text: Volunteers commit to at least one hour a week for four months or one school semester. Placements are set with a site supervisor.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer application, then take a 20-minute screening call. The application form is closed for now because the program is at capacity, so check back.
first_step.basis: Needs an application, a screening call and background checks, and the form is closed with no reopening date.

records.notes: Run by the city's Office of Innovation and Technology, launched January 29, 2026. Application form temporarily closed (at capacity) as of this check. Youth volunteers 14 to 17 need a parent's permission. Background checks, including a PA child abuse clearance for youth or library and rec sites, are required. Owner may want to recheck when the form reopens.

leads_only.name: Philly Full Moon Ride
leads_only.note: Cycling group, not in this family. Named as Best Cycling Club in a 2026 Philadelphia magazine roundup. Instagram only, so not checked.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Robotics Coalition
leads_only.note: Named in a search result as supporting school robotics teams. The coverage said its school district funding was set to end in September 2024. No website link found in search; needs a current check.

leads_only.name: Philly Hardware Meetup
leads_only.note: Named in a 2022 Technical.ly article as a monthly or bimonthly meetup. No website link found; likely dormant, needs a current check.

leads_only.name: Frankford Radio Club
leads_only.note: Ham radio club named in a CBS Philadelphia article, members from Philadelphia and nearby. Date unclear; no website link found.

leads_only.name: Holmesburg Amateur Radio Club
leads_only.note: Named in 2007 club minutes with a repeater on High Rise South. No current evidence found; no website link.

notes: Making-tech lane had few current groups with their own sites. Records: 7 checked. Verdicts: publish 7 (6 active or probably active, 1 dormant with low confidence). Dropped with reasons: Code for Philly (codeforphilly.org returned only its page title on three fetches, so no facts could be recorded); Philly CoderDojo (phillycoderdojo.org did not resolve, so no second guess); Skidmarks MC (skidmarksmc.com did not resolve); Maker Faire Philly (a yearly event, April 2026 already held, not a group); 300M Club (car club based outside Philadelphia, about two hours away at Carlisle, so out of area); NW Philly Repair Cafe run by Time4Time Community Exchange (only dated evidence is a May 2015 article, so no current status; website not found); Penn W3ABT amateur radio club (only 2006 to 2009 minutes found, no current evidence); Coded by Kids (only 2014 evidence). Illegal street car meetups in the search results were not recorded. Car and motorcycle gap: no legitimate Philadelphia-based community car or motorcycle club with a checkable website was found; Iron Order Death Grip chapter and Covered Bridge charity ride (Levittown start, Bucks County) were not checked. Searches used: 9 of 10. Fetches used: 19.
